questions.question: Which of the following symbols refers to programs, applications, or a shortcut to an item, file, or program on a computer in Windows XP?

__
 
• An **icon** in Windows XP represents programs, applications, or shortcuts to items, files, or programs on a computer.
 
• Icons are small graphical representations that help users quickly identify and access various types of content on their computer.
 
• Icons typically appear on the **desktop** or within file directories, making it easy to launch applications or open files with a double-click.
 
• In Windows XP, icons can be customized with different **images** to represent different types of files or programs.
 
• Users can also create **shortcuts** to programs or files, which are represented by icons with a small arrow in the corner.

 __
 
• The **taskbar** is a graphical element at the bottom of the screen in Windows XP.
 
• It contains the **Start button, system tray, and open application windows**.
 
• The taskbar helps users manage and switch between open applications and windows.
 
 
 
• **Path**__
 __
 
• A **path** refers to the specific location or address of a file or folder in a computer's file system.
 
• It is typically written as a series of directories separated by backslashes (e.g., C:\Program Files\).
 
• Paths help users and programs locate specific files within the storage hierarchy of the computer.
 
 
 
• **Start button**__
 
 
• The **Start button** is located on the taskbar and provides access to the Start menu.
 
• The Start menu includes shortcuts to programs, folders, and system settings.
 
• It is the primary way to access installed applications and system functions in Windows XP.

• Hence, Tamil Nadu receives most of its rain from north east and **retreating monsoons **__during winter season.
 
• Moreover, many low pressure systems develop in the** Bay of Bengal during this period and move towards the east coast of Tamil Nadu** causing heavy rainfall.

• During the winter season, the **winds prevailing** in the country are the **Northeast trade winds.**
 
• In major parts of the country, it is a** dry season,** as the winds blow from** land to sea.**
 
• When the winds blow from sea to land, it picks up **moisture from the sea and brings rainfall **to the country.

questions.question: ________ is used to control the demand and supply of money.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Credit control.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Credit control** is used to control the** demand and supply of money.** 
 
• Credit control refers to the actions taken by the **central bank or monetary authority** to regulate the **availability and cost of credit** in the economy.
 
• By controlling the availability of credit, the central bank can influence the demand for money and therefore** control the money supply.**
 
• Credit control is important for maintaining **price stability and preventing inflation.**
 
• If the central bank allows too much credit to be available, it can lead to an **increase in demand for goods and services**, which can cause prices to rise.
 
• By controlling credit, the central bank can** prevent this** from happening.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• One of the main tools used in credit control is the **setting of interest rates.**
 
• By increasing or decreasing interest rates, the central bank can make** credit more or less expensive**, which can influence the demand for money and the money supply.
 
• Other tools used in credit control include **reserve requirements, open market operations, and moral suasion.**
 
• **Reserve requirements** refer to the amount of money that banks are required to** hold in reserve, **which can influence the amount of credit they can lend.
 
• **Open market operations** involve the** buying and selling of government securities**, which can influence the amount of money in circulation.
 
• **Moral suasion **refers to the **use of persuasion and influence** to encourage banks to adopt certain policies or practices.
 
• **Equity control **refers to the **regulation of ownership** in companies and other assets. 
 
• It is not directly related to the **supply and demand of money.**

questions.question: When was the restructuring of public distribution system as a targeted public distribution system?
questions.solution:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The restructuring of the public distribution system as the **targeted public distribution system** (TPDS) was implemented in **1997**.
 
• The TPDS aims to provide food grains to the poor at subsidized rates, ensuring food security for the most vulnerable sections of society.
 
• Under TPDS, households are classified into **Below Poverty Line** (BPL) and **Above Poverty Line** (APL) categories, with BPL families receiving higher subsidies.
 
• This system was introduced to enhance the efficiency of the public distribution system by targeting the benefits more accurately to those in need.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The public distribution system in India has been in existence since the Second World War and was expanded in the 1960s and 1970s as a universal scheme.
 
• The TPDS was **introduced as part of the economic reforms of the 1990s** to address inefficiencies and leakages in the universal public distribution system.
 
• State governments are responsible for identifying eligible families and distributing food grains through a network of fair price shops.
 
• Over the years, various measures, including the use of technology, have been implemented to improve transparency and reduce corruption in the TPDS.

questions.question: A galvanometer when connected in a circuit, detects the presence of:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Current**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A **galvanometer** is an instrument used to detect and measure small **electric currents** in a circuit.
 
• It works based on the principle of **electromagnetic deflection**, where a current-carrying coil experiences a torque in a magnetic field.
 
• The deflection of the needle in a galvanometer is directly proportional to the amount of current flowing through it.
 
• Galvanometers are primarily used in laboratories and electrical experiments to check the presence and direction of **current**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The working of a galvanometer is based on the **Motor Principle**, where a current-carrying conductor placed in a magnetic field experiences a force.
 
• A galvanometer consists of a moving coil suspended in a magnetic field, and the deflection is observed on a calibrated scale.
 
• It is different from an **ammeter**, which is a modified galvanometer designed to measure larger currents with negligible resistance.
 
• For detecting **potential difference**, a voltmeter is used, and for measuring **resistance**, an ohmmeter is employed.
 
• Modern galvanometers have been replaced by digital multimeters in many practical applications, but they are still used for precision measurements in labs.
 
• One common type of galvanometer is the **moving coil galvanometer**, which is widely used due to its high sensitivity and accuracy.

questions.question: In South Indian temple architecture, what is the name of the stepped or pyramidal structure built above the sanctum?

__
 
• In South Indian temple architecture, the term **Vimana** refers to the **pyramidal or stepped structure** built directly above the sanctum (garbhagriha).
 
• The Vimana is often elaborately decorated with intricate carvings, sculptures, and ornamental details, showcasing the artistic skill of ancient Indian craftsmen.
 
• This feature is a distinguishing aspect of Dravidian temple architecture, commonly seen in temples of Tamil Nadu, Andhra Pradesh, Karnataka, and Kerala.
 
• The Vimana serves not only as an architectural feature but also as a symbolic representation of the sacred Mount Meru, believed to be the center of the universe in Hindu cosmology.
 
• Famous examples of Vimanas can be seen in temples like the **Brihadeeswarar Temple** in Thanjavur and the **Meenakshi Temple** in Madurai.

• **Jagati:**
 
 
• The Jagati refers to a raised platform that surrounds the temple, often used for circumambulation (pradakshina) by devotees.
 
 
 
• **Mandapa:**
 
 
• A Mandapa is a pillared hall or pavilion in a temple, used for congregational purposes, rituals, and ceremonies. It is often located in front of the sanctum.
 
 
 
• **South Indian Temple Architecture:**
 
 
• South Indian temples are primarily built in the Dravidian architectural style, characterized by towering gopurams (gateway towers), Vimanas, and intricate carvings.
 
• The temple layout often includes key components like the Garbhagriha (sanctum), Vimana, Mandapa, and Prakara (enclosure walls).

⇒ √(1 + √(8 + √(8 + x))) = 2

Squaring both sides to remove the outermost square root:

⇒ 1 + √(8 + √(8 + x)) = 2²

⇒ 1 + √(8 + √(8 + x)) = 4

⇒ √(8 + √(8 + x)) = 4 − 1

⇒ √(8 + √(8 + x)) = 3

Squaring both sides again:

⇒ 8 + √(8 + x) = 3²

questions.question: 44 pipes can fill a large water tank in 27 hours. How many hours will it take for 66 pipes to fill four such tanks?

⇒ 44 × 27 / 1 = 66 × H₂ / 4

⇒ H₂ = (44 × 27 × 4) ÷ 66

Pipes & Cisterns

All pipes of identical size fill a tank at the exact same rate. Their combined efficiency is directly proportional to the total number of active pipes.

questions.question: Find the remainder when 2³² is divided by 5.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Using Euler's Totient Theorem: if a and n are coprime, aφ⁽ⁿ⁾ mod n = 1.

For prime n = 5, the totient φ(5) = 5 − 1 = 4.

Since 2 and 5 are coprime, 2⁴ mod 5 = 1.

We need to find the remainder for 2³², which can be written as (2⁴)⁸.

⇒ Remainder = (2⁴)⁸ mod 5 = 1⁸ mod 5 = 1.

**∴ The correct answer is 1.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Expression = 2³² ÷ 5

**Method Used:**

Using the negative remainder concept:

(ax − 1)eveⁿ ÷ a leaves a remainder of 1.

**Calculation:**

⇒ 2³² can be written in powers of 2 that are close to a multiple of 5.

⇒ 2³² = (2²)¹⁶ = 4¹⁶

Now, we divide 4¹⁶ by 5.

⇒ Remainder = 4¹⁶ ÷ 5

⇒ Remainder = (5 − 1)¹⁶ ÷ 5

Using the remainder theorem, the remainder depends only on the (−1) part.

⇒ Remainder = (−1)¹⁶

Since 16 is an even power, a negative number multiplied an even number of times yields a positive result.

⇒ Remainder = 1

**∴ The correct answer is 1.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Fermat's Little Theorem

If p is a prime number, then for any integer a, ap−¹ mod p = 1. This theorem is highly useful for directly finding remainders of large exponents when divided by prime numbers.

Binomial Remainder Theorem

When (x + a)ⁿ is divided by x, the remainder is aⁿ. Similarly, for (x − 1)ⁿ ÷ x, the remainder is 1 if n is even, and (x − 1) if n is odd.

Cyclicity of Remainders

The remainders of powers of a number follow a repeating sequence when divided by a fixed divisor. Finding the cycle length allows reducing extremely large exponents into easily calculable single-digit powers.
</p

questions.question: Three numbers are in the ratio of 3 ∶ 4 ∶ 5 respectively and their LCM is 2,400. Their H.C.F. is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Since the given ratio parts 3, 4, and 5 are co-prime, their LCM is simply their product: 3 × 4 × 5 = 60.

The total LCM of the numbers is equal to their H.C.F multiplied by the LCM of their ratios.

⇒ Total LCM = H.C.F × (LCM of ratios)

⇒ 2400 = H.C.F × 60

⇒ H.C.F = 2400 ÷ 60 = 40

**∴ The correct answer is 40.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Ratio of the three numbers = 3 : 4 : 5

LCM of the three numbers = 2400

**Formula Used:**

If numbers are in the ratio a : b : c, then the numbers can be written as ax, bx, and cx, where x is their highest common factor (H.C.F).

The LCM of ax, bx, and cx is given by x × LCM(a, b, c).

 
• 
• 
• 
• 
• 
• H.C.F = x 1st = 3x 2nd = 4x 3rd = 5x LCM = 60x = 2400 x = 40 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the three numbers be 3x, 4x, and 5x, where x is their H.C.F.

⇒ The LCM of the ratio parts 3, 4, and 5 is 60.

⇒ Hence, the LCM of the three numbers 3x, 4x, and 5x is 60x.

⇒ It is given that the total LCM is 2400.

⇒ 60x = 2400

⇒ x = 2400 ÷ 60

⇒ x = 40

⇒ Therefore, the H.C.F of the given numbers is 40.

**∴ The correct answer is 40.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Relation between H.C.F and LCM (For two numbers)

For any two numbers 'a' and 'b', the product of the numbers is equal to the product of their H.C.F and LCM (a × b = H.C.F × LCM). Note that this general formula is exclusively applicable to two numbers only.

Co-prime Numbers

Two or more numbers are called co-prime if their H.C.F is 1. When numbers are reduced to their simplest ratio form, the individual ratio parts become co-prime to each other.

H.C.F and LCM of Fractions

H.C.F of fractions = (H.C.F of numerators) ÷ (LCM of denominators).

LCM of fractions = (LCM of numerators) ÷ (H.C.F of denominators).

questions.question: If (x²+(1)/(x²))=18 and x > 1, what is the value of (x³-(1)/(x³))?

If x − 1/x = a, then x³ − 1/x³ = a³ + 3a.

⇒ x³ − 1/x³ = (x − 1/x)³ + 3(x)(1/x)(x − 1/x)

⇒ x³ − 1/x³ = 4³ + 3 × 4

⇒ x³ − 1/x³ = 64 + 12

Result = −1 + 1 = 0.

**∴ The correct answer is 0.**

sec(180° − θ) = −sec θ

cosec(180° − θ) = cosec θ

cos θ × sec θ = 1

sin θ × cosec θ = 1

⇒ sec 133° = sec(180° − 47°) = −sec 47°

⇒ cosec 136° = cosec(180° − 44°) = cosec 44°

In the 2ⁿd quadrant (90° to 180°), only Sine (sin) and Cosecant (cosec) are positive. Cosine (cos), Secant (sec), Tangent (tan), and Cotangent (cot) are negative.

Angles that add up to 180° are supplementary. sin(180° − θ) = sin θ, while cos(180° − θ) = −cos θ.

questions.question: A trader buys two articles for Rs. 3,000 each. While selling, he earns a 10 percent profit on one and loses 20 percent on the other. What will be his overall loss percentage?

When the Cost Price (CP) of two articles is the same, the overall profit or loss percentage is the simple average of the individual profit and loss percentages.

Overall % = (Profit % − Loss %) ÷ 2

The negative sign indicates an overall loss of 5%.

**∴ The correct answer is 5 percent.**

Profit on first article = 10%

Loss on second article = 20%

When Cost Prices are Equal

questions.question: Find the mean proportional between 3 and 27.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The mean proportional between two numbers 'a' and 'b' is given directly by √(a × b).

Here, the given numbers are a = 3 and b = 27.

Mean proportional = √(3 × 27) = √81 = 9.

**∴ The correct answer is 9.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

The two numbers are 3 and 27.

**Formula Used:**

If x is the mean proportional between a and b, then a : x :: x : b.

By the property of proportions, Product of Means = Product of Extremes ⇒ x² = a × b.

 Product of Means = Product of Extremes
 
 3
 :
 
 x
 ::
 
 x
 :
 
 27
 

 Extremes
 

 Means
 x × x = 3 × 27 = 81
 Result: x = 9

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the required mean proportional be x.

⇒ 3 : x :: x : 27

⇒ 3 ÷ x = x ÷ 27

⇒ x² = 3 × 27

⇒ x² = 81

⇒ x = √81 = 9

**∴ The correct answer is 9.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Third Proportional

If three quantities a, b, and c are in continued proportion (a : b :: b : c), then 'c' is the third proportional to a and b. Formula: c = b² ÷ a.

Fourth Proportional

If four quantities a, b, c, and d are in proportion (a : b :: c : d), then 'd' is the fourth proportional to a, b, and c. Formula: d = (b × c) ÷ a.

Duplicate Ratio

The duplicate ratio of any two numbers a and b is simply the ratio of their squares, expressed mathematically as a² : b².

Sub-duplicate Ratio

The sub-duplicate ratio of any two numbers a and b is the ratio of their square roots, expressed mathematically as √a : √b.

questions.question: If 29 @ 12 = 34, 57 @ 38 = 38, 45 @ 29 = 32, then 67 @ 49 = ?
questions.solution:
The given relations are of the form:

First number @ Second number = Third number

The pattern followed here is:

**(First number - Second number) × 2 = Third number**

For example, in 29 @ 12,

(29 - 12) × 2 = 17 × 2

⇒ 34

In 57 @ 38 = 38

(57 - 38) × 2 = 19 × 2

= 38

In 45 @ 29 = 32

(45 - 29) × 2 = 16 × 2

= 32

Similarly,

In 67 @ 49,

(67 - 49) × 2 = 18 × 2

⇒ **36**

Hence, **"36"** is the result of '67 @ 49'.

**Given:**

Paulo's rank from the top = 18th

Paulo's rank from the bottom = 45th

**Formula Used:**

Total number of students in a class = (Rank from top + Rank from bottom) - 1

**Calculations:**

Total number of students = (18 + 45) - 1

⇒ Total number of students = 63 - 1

⇒ Total number of students = 62

**∴ The total number of students in the class is 62.**

Hence, the correct answer is "Option 3".
